title: Take a Bow: Taylor Swift’s ‘The Life Of A Showgirl’ Returns to No. 1 In Australia
summary: Thanks to the release of the "Encore" edition, "Showgirl" returns to No. 1 and new release "Patient Zero" tops the singles chart.
body: There’s a lot of life left in Taylor Swift ’s Showgirl , as the pop superstar’s 2025 album returns to No. 1 in Australia and one of its fresh cuts leads the national singles survey. Thanks to the release of the “Encore” edition, a deluxe set introducing the tracks “Patient Zero,” “Pink Clouding,” “Babylon” and “Cleveland!,” The Life Of A Showgirl (via Republic/Universal) powers 23-1 on the ARIA Albums Chart . With its return to the chart spotlight, Showgirl makes a notable impression on the ARIA Singles Chart , too, with “Patient Zero” debuting at No. 1 for a TayTay chart double. In the process, Swift dethrones Ella Langley ’s four-time platinum country smash “Choosin’ Texas” (Sony), down 1-2. Close behind is Swift’s “Cleveland!” (at No. 3), “Babylon” (No. 4) and “Pink Clouding” (No. 5), and Showgirl’s lead single “The Fate of Ophelia” bounces 14-10 (“Ophelia” logged six weeks at No. 1 in October and November). Swift has now accumulated 69 top 10 hits on the ARIA Singles Chart, the charts compiler reports. “Patient Zero” is her second leader this year in Australia, after “I Knew It, I Knew You” from Toy …

title: Not even the NVIDIA Shield TV Pro is safe from a huge price hike
summary: It looks like we've got another casualty of the RAM crisis.
body: Credit: Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority TL;DR The NVIDIA Shield TV Pro has received a ~$100 price hike on Amazon and Best Buy. The streaming box now costs ~$300 via these platforms. We’re guessing this price hike is due to the RAM crisis, which has raised memory costs across the board. The NVIDIA Shield TV Pro is still one of the best Android TV boxes around, over a decade after its initial release. That’s due to its respectable level of horsepower, an array of features, and a long update commitment. Unfortunately, it looks like even this venerable TV box isn’t safe from price increases. NVIDIA may have stealthily raised the price of the Shield TV Pro. The TV box is now listed at $300.26 on Amazon and $299.99 on Best Buy (h/t: r/ShieldAndroidTV ). This would be a ~$100 increase over the previous $200 asking price.

title: Google Meet and Microsoft Teams just got better at working together
summary: Your meeting room no longer has to pick a side.
body: TL;DR Google Meet and Microsoft Teams can now work across supported Android-based meeting-room hardware. Meet hardware can join Teams calls, while Android-based Microsoft Teams Rooms can join Google Meet meetings. The feature began rolling out on October 1 and should reach eligible Google Workspace customers within 1-3 days. If you’ve ever walked into a meeting room only to realize the call is on Microsoft Teams while the room is set up for Google Meet , you’ll know how unnecessarily complicated something as simple as joining a video call can become. Google started addressing that problem last month when it previewed a new interoperability feature that would let Meet and Teams hardware work together. The idea was to remove some of the usual barriers between the two platforms. With the feature, a meeting room equipped with Android-based Google Meet hardware could join a Microsoft Teams call, while a Microsoft Teams Room running Android could do the same with a Google Meet call. So, if your company primarily uses Meet but a client sends you a Teams invite, you wouldn’t have to reach for a laptop or switch rooms just because everyone happens to be using a different video conferencing…

title: A strange YouTube login bug is locking some users out of the website
summary: Reports suggest an account-specific sign-in bug could be affecting multiple browsers.
body: TL;DR Some YouTube users can’t sign in on web browsers, even though their Google accounts work normally elsewhere. Reports span multiple browsers and computers, with affected accounts still working in the YouTube mobile and TV apps. The issue has been escalated for investigation, but Google hasn’t publicly explained what’s causing it or when a fix may arrive. YouTube only recently put out one login fire after fixing a bug that locked some viewers out on TVs and gaming consoles . But while that problem was getting attention, another sign-in headache appears to have been quietly frustrating a much smaller group of YouTube users on the web. Reports stretching back roughly two weeks describe accounts that work normally across other Google services but refuse to sign in to YouTube in a browser. A Reddit user said clearing cookies, switching browsers, using Incognito mode, changing passwords, and even trying another computer made no difference. Their affected accounts still worked in YouTube’s mobile app.

The book is a spirited, heartwarming story that follows Pan Dorobo (literally, “bread thief”) after they arrive on the freezing Buruburu Island. title: Google Messages is having trouble sending media files over RCS
summary: Google Messages is refusing to send media to other Android phones.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Android users are having trouble sending media to other Android phones on Google Messages. The affected users claim that GIFs, pictures, photomoji, and stickers are not delivered when RCS is enabled. There are reportedly no issues when sending media to an iPhone via RCS. Google Messages just took a step closer to supporting a long-desired feature, RCS video calls . While it’s still very much a work in progress, it’s nice to know that it’s something that could come down the road. But before Google even thinks about rolling out such a feature, it will need to iron out a new wrinkle that’s causing trouble with media sent over RCS. Over on Reddit ( 1 , 2 , 3 ), users are reporting an issue with Google Messages. When RCS is enabled in the app, these users are unable to send media files to other Android phones, such as GIFs, pictures, photomoji, and stickers. It appears that switching to SMS/MMS solves the problem for most of the affected users.

title: The Galaxy S26 price increase we were dreading is here
summary: All models of the Galaxy S26 series are now pricier by $100, while the 1TB Galaxy S26 Ultra sees an even larger increase.
body: TL;DR Samsung has raised prices for the Galaxy S26 series in the US and South Korea due to the global shortage of memory components. While 256GB and 512GB variants have seen a $100 price increase in the US, the 1TB Galaxy S26 Ultra model costs $200 more. While we’re still seeing some online listings that show the older price tag, that may not last long. The global shortage of memory components has widely impacted the tech industry. We recently came across a report suggesting Samsung was about to raise the price of the Galaxy S26 series on October 1 . With the day finally here, the manufacturer has officially increased the prices of the Galaxy S26 series in the US and South Korea. A quick look at the Samsung US website reveals a $100 price bump across the 256GB and 512GB variants of the Galaxy S26, Galaxy S26 Plus, and the Galaxy S26 Ultra. This means the cheapest Galaxy S26 version now starts at $999.99, while the Galaxy S26 Plus and Ultra start at $1,199.99 and $1,399.99, respectively. Meanwhile, the Galaxy S26 Ultra in the 1TB configuration will cost $200 more, bringing it to $1,999.99.

title: Android could soon let you trigger Emergency SOS without touching your phone at all

body: Credit: Roydon Cerejo / Android Authority TL;DR Google is developing a hands-free Emergency SOS trigger for Android devices. Google’s Personal Safety is an extremely useful app that lets users share their whereabouts with loved ones, get alerts about extreme weather, or raise an alarm using the Emergency SOS feature. On Pixel phones and watches, this app also handles features such as Fall Detection and Crash Detection. Currently, triggering an Emergency SOS , especially on non-Pixel devices, requires users to physically press the power button five times. But now it seems like Google may be adding another way to trigger it even without touching the phone.

summary: It gets compact cards, a refreshed look for the TV remote, and a floating navigation bar.
body: TL;DR Samsung has started rolling out the redesigned SmartThings app to Android devices. The update brings a compact layout for cards and support for resizing and rearranging device and routine cards. The built-in TV remote now comes with a light mode option, and users can also resize or reposition it. Samsung rolled out the redesigned SmartThings app a couple of days ago. Surprisingly, however, the update went out to iOS devices before it even arrived on Samsung’s own smartphones. Now, the refreshed SmartThings app is finally hitting Android devices. The redesign appears to be rolling out with version 1.8.51.30 of the SmartThings app and looks nearly identical to the iOS build. The navigation bar now features a floating appearance, and the interface adopts a more compact layout for device and routine cards.

title: Google Antigravity looks like an Android app, but your phone isn’t invited
summary: We put Google Antigravity on a Pixel phone to see how far it would get.
body: TL;DR Google Antigravity is now listed in the Play Store, but it’s built for Googlebooks rather than regular Android phones. We sideloaded the app on a Pixel phone, where its interface was poorly scaled, and setup failed during Terminal VM configuration. Googlebook OS uses the Android stack, so the Play Store may increasingly include apps that look like Android apps but only work on Googlebooks. Seeing an app in the Google Play Store usually comes with a pretty safe assumption: your Android phone can probably run it. But Google’s new Antigravity listing reminds us that the Googlebook OS is about to make that assumption a lot less reliable. Antigravity has now landed on Google Play, but despite the familiar storefront, this is very much a Googlebook app — and our attempt to force it onto a Pixel phone went nowhere. The Play Store listing itself gives the game away as soon as you open it on the web. Google describes Antigravity as an agent-first development platform that can create and deploy apps directly on a Googlebook, with agents able to write, edit, and manage code, projects, and files locally. Google Play also marks regular Android devices as incompatible, which explains why …

The smart display is said to come with a six-inch square screen featuring dynamic facial and voice user recognition, and an OS combining elements of iPadOS, watchOS, and StandBy mode from iOS. The new hardware could capitalize on user frustration with Google Home automation bugs and compromises on the Pixel Tablet. For years, Google and Amazon have dominated the smart home space, with Apple largely sitting on the sidelines. While Apple offered the HomePod and HomePod mini, its lack of a dedicated smart display left Cupertino lagging behind the best smart home ecosystems. Meanwhile, Google has had plenty of runway with the Nest Hub, Nest Hub Max , and its ambitious dockable Pixel Tablet . However, this smart home journey hasn’t been smooth of late, with plenty of complaints arising from Google’s and Amazon’s AI integrations. The room is wide open for disruption, and Apple could be planning to do exactly that this month with new smart home hardware. According to a Blo…

body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Huawei has indicated it plans to increase phone prices, responding to pressure from increasing memory and component costs. This follows a series of hikes from multiple phone brands, including Apple, Samsung, and Google. Huawei also predicts a tough time for the smartphone industry overall, noting that budget offerings will be hit hardest. The impact of rising component costs on consumer electronics doesn’t seem to be softening and could soon envelop more brands. After several phone brands, including Apple , Google , and Samsung , have raised prices on their newest models, Huawei is reportedly on the same track. Huawei’s chairman of consumer business, Richard Yu, recently told Chinese media that it expects to raise prices for its products, but only to a “moderate” extent. Yu was quoted by the media (via Bloomberg ) as saying the company has been absorbing added costs of about $200, and that has been “hurting” its “profitability very badly.” Yu’s statement came alongside the launch of Huawei’s flagship Mate 90 series, which includes a special edition model going as high as CNY 18,999 (~$2,835) as well as a detachable camera with its …

title: Google’s bizarre new Gboard keyboard is a conveyor belt that brings the keys to you
summary: You can actually build this thing yourself.
body: Credit: Google TL;DR Google Japan has unveiled a DIY Gboard keyboard with keys mounted on a moving conveyor belt. Instead of moving your hand around a traditional keyboard, you can simply wait for the key you want to type to roll past. You can’t buy it, but Google has published the blueprints as open source, so you can actually build one. Google has once again decided that keyboards are far too normal. For its annual October 1 tradition, the company’s Japanese division has unveiled a new DIY Gboard keyboard that takes a rather bizarre approach — moving the keys to you instead of making you move your fingers to them.

They also bring Galaxy AI features such as access to Gemini Live, Quick Voice Memo, and head gestures, with a Korean launch set for October 27 at 299,000 won and a global rollout to follow. Samsung has quietly launched the Galaxy Buds On, its first clip-on wireless earbuds under the Galaxy Buds branding. The new wireless earbuds were quietly unveiled alongside the US launch of the Galaxy Tab S12 series and SmartTag 3 , although Samsung didn’t give them the same fanfare as its other new hardware.

body: TL;DR Plex is rolling out social features to the Android TV app. Users can now discuss, rate, react, and more. The primary menu has been relocated to the left-hand side of the screen. Tired of having an algorithm telling you what to watch next? Plex is bringing a human touch to content discovery. New social tools could help you find the next show you want to invest your time in. Today, Plex is rolling out social features to Android TV. These features include Discussions, Lists, Reviews, Reactions, and Follows. title: Gemini for Home is now better at hearing you in noisy rooms

body: TL;DR Google Home’s third September update makes Gemini for Home better at hearing commands in noisy rooms and responding faster. The app also improves Find My Phone reliability, multilingual recognition, smart light controls, camera tiles, and device setup. A long list of fixes targets Matter switches, Favorites tiles, camera playback, Onn camera history, and Automations. Polishing the Google Home app is a clear priority for Google, and that’s evident in the sheer number of updates the company pushes out for the app . To round off September, Google Home is getting yet another update — the third update this month. After rolling out better combined media and smart home commands, followed by another round of fixes that improved camera reliability and widget efficiency, Google is now making the Home app faster, more reliable, and better at hearing your commands.

Both styles of intelligent eyewear will have multiple variants. Samsung has long been working on smart glasses that can go toe-to-toe with Meta’s offerings. We got a taste of what to expect earlier this year, during the company’s summer Unpacked event. Similar to how Meta partnered with Ray-Ban, Samsung is teaming up with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster for the design. While there’s still more to learn about these smart glasses, FCC listings are providing some new information. One is presumably for the pair from Warby Parker, and the other from Gentle Monster.

title: This camera company is taking over Google Photos’ Print Store
summary: The core experience stays the same.
body: TL;DR Fujifilm is taking over Google Photos’ existing Print Store in the US. The store is now co-branded as Fujifilm for Google Photos Print Store, with Fujifilm handling operations, support, and the product catalog. Users still access printing through Google Photos. They’re getting more print formats, frames, décor, gifts, and select in-store pickup options. In addition to being your media storage gallery , Google Photos also acts as a gateway to the tech giant’s Print Store . It lets you order things like photo prints, photo books, and canvas prints directly from the app and the web, making it a convenient platform to turn your digital memories into physical ones. Functionality-wise, nothing is changing here. But there’s still a notable change behind the scenes that you should know about. The Google Photos Print Store is now being operated by Fujifilm , the company best known for making cameras.

But just because those doors are open doesn’t mean that users will get the same experience everywhere, and it’s not uncommon to see a bit of disparity. Apple Music has been on Android for over a decade now, but lately the Android app has felt like it’s lacking some of the polish of its iOS sibling. That’s now starting to at least get a little better, with the release of Apple Music 7.0 for Android. Over on X, user Sumanta Das gave us a heads-up that the app’s new look was rolling out. body: Credit: Mobvoi TL;DR Mobvoi has announced the launch of the TicNote Watch. This smartwatch is built to capture, transcribe, and summarize conversations without the need for a smartphone. The TicNote Watch costs $249, but it will be available for $199 for a limited time. Mobvoi, maker of the TicWatch, is back with a brand new smartwatch . The company has announced the launch of the TicNote Watch. However, this new digital timepiece is a little different from its previous offerings, as it’s designed with a specific audience in mind. The TicNote Watch’s main purpose revolves around conversations. It’s built to be a note-taking companion, capable of capturing, transcribing, and summarizing conversations without a smartphone. The device also offers typical smartwatch features, but the focus is on AI-powered note-taking. As a result, the TicNote Watch’s key demographic is meeting-intensive professionals, such as journalists, healthcare providers, consultants, and so on.

title: You can now turn your Android handheld into a Steam Deck, and here’s the proof
summary: It's still early days, but this is impressive nonetheless.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR Valve has released Steam OS for Arm following the release of its Arm-powered Steam Frame headset. Developers have subsequently ported this version of Steam OS to Android handhelds. We were able to run Steam OS on an AYN handheld, yielding a Steam Deck-like experience. Ever wanted to run Steam games on your Android handheld ? There’s no shortage of ways to do so, such as Android apps like GameNative and Winlator. We also installed the Rocknix Linux distribution on our Android handheld earlier this year, which includes an official Arm version of Steam. But what if you actually want to install the Steam Deck’s OS on your device? We now have some good news. Valve recently released Steam OS for Arm devices. This isn’t a surprise as its newly launched Steam Frame VR headset runs on an Arm-based Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 chipset. It’s basically a VR headset powered by a phone’s internals.

title: Samsung launches Galaxy Tab S12 series, and the base model is nowhere to be found
summary: The Plus model is back.
body: TL;DR Samsung’s Galaxy Tab S12 series drops the base model and brings back the Plus, alongside the 14.6-inch Ultra. Both tablets get thinner designs, Dimensity 9500 power, 120Hz AMOLED displays, new AI/multitasking features, and up to 23 hours of video playback. The Galaxy Tab S12 Plus starts at $1,199.99, while the Tab S12 Ultra starts at $1,399.99, with availability beginning October 7. Samsung is one of the biggest players in the tablet market , and it clearly doesn’t want to lose its seat at the big table. To ensure that, the tech giant seems to be making a small adjustment to its flagship tablet strategy with the latest Tab S12 series. For reference, with last year’s Tab S11 series , Samsung decided to skip the mid-sized Plus model in favor of the Tab S11 and Tab S11 Ultra. This year, Samsung is walking back on that decision and bringing the Plus model back, but, of course, there’s a trade-off: There’s no base model.

The phones could apparently get higher prices “across various storage capacities and models.” It’s believed that the price hikes could range from ~$74 to ~$96 in Korea. The RAM crisis is showing no signs of abating, as AI companies greedily buy up memory and other key components. This has resulted in higher prices for consumer electronics, with even Samsung forced to increase the price of its smartphones in 2026. Now, we’ve got more details about Samsung’s apparent price strategy for the Galaxy S27 series . title: This Android brand just launched its own e-reader that lives on the back of your phone
summary: The 3.68-inch ePaper reader weighs just 61g and snaps onto almost any phone.
body: TL;DR HONOR has quietly introduced the Life S3, a tiny 3.68-inch E Ink reader that magnetically attaches to the back of a phone. It weighs 61g, supports Wi-Fi 6 for book transfers and microSD cards up to 1TB, and promises up to 30 hours of reading. HONOR isn’t the first phone brand to experiment with E Ink accessories, but the S3 stands out as a standalone reader that can work with virtually any phone. ePaper displays and smartphones have crossed paths plenty of times before. The YotaPhone famously put an ePaper screen right on the back of a handset, while HUAWEI once offered an optional ePaper rear cover for the P8. More recently, gadgets like the magnetic Flowtica Verso have turned the back of your phone into useful accessory space. HONOR is now giving that old idea a bookish twist with the HONOR Life S3, a tiny, standalone e-reader designed to hitch a ride on your phone. According to a JD.com listing (spotted via Michael Yang Eink Lab ), the HONOR Life S3 has a 3.68-inch ePaper touchscreen with a 259ppi pixel density, packed into a 5.6mm-thick body weighing 61g. It has no front light, though, so you’ll need ambient light for nighttime reading.

Google has long pitched virtual try-on as a viable way to get non-savvy users to use AI. Earlier in September, Google also included the option to import your own outfits from existing photos and try them virtually against a neutral background, with a more stoic pose. The feature has its quirks , but Google is testing new options to expand it and address some of the limitations. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. title: How I freed up 15GB on my Samsung Galaxy phone using 3 tools — and why you only need one
